zh.principle: **攻击**：推测执行侧信道（Speculative Execution Side-Channel）。Meltdown 论文摘要给出的机制是：「Meltdown exploits side effects of out-of-order execution on modern processors to read arbitrary kernel-memory locations including personal data and passwords」，并说明「Out-of-order execution is an indispensable performance feature and present in a wide range of modern processors」——性能特性本身的副作用被用作观察通道。
zh.why: 摘要把根因定位在硬件而非软件：「The root cause of Meltdown is the hardware.The attack is independent of the operating system, and it does not rely on any software vulnerabilities.」，因此隔离失效不是某个程序的缺陷；摘要还说明在受影响系统上「Meltdown enables an adversary to read memory of other processes or virtual machines in the cloud without any permissions or privileges」。
zh.used: 该论文同时给出部署结论：「We show that the KAISER defense mechanism for KASLR has the important (but inadvertent) side effect of impeding Meltdown.We stress that KAISER must be deployed immediately…」——即文中所称针对 KASLR 的 KAISER 防御机制顺带阻碍了该攻击，论文的部署结论是 KAISER 必须立即部署。
zh.broken: 摘要对影响面只作有限声明：「The attack works on different Intel microarchitectures since at least 2010 and potentially other processors are affected」——文中点名的是 Intel 微架构，其他厂商只是`可能被影响`的表述；该条目据此不使用超出摘要范围的厂商结论。攻击的成立也依赖可被推测执行的乱序机制，因此无法通过软件漏洞修补，只能靠部署隔离与硬件修正。

en.principle: **Attack**: Speculative Execution Side-Channel (推测执行侧信道). The Meltdown abstract gives the mechanism: "Meltdown exploits side effects of out-of-order execution on modern processors to read arbitrary kernel-memory locations including personal data and passwords", and notes that "Out-of-order execution is an indispensable performance feature and present in a wide range of modern processors" — the side effects of a performance feature become the observation channel.
en.why: The abstract places the root cause in hardware rather than software: "The root cause of Meltdown is the hardware. The attack is independent of the operating system, and it does not rely on any software vulnerabilities." The isolation failure is therefore not a bug in one program, and on affected systems "Meltdown enables an adversary to read memory of other processes or virtual machines in the cloud without any permissions or privileges".
en.used:
The paper also delivers a deployment conclusion: "We show that the KAISER defense mechanism for KASLR has the important (but inadvertent) side effect of impeding Meltdown. We stress that KAISER must be deployed immediately…" — what the abstract calls the KAISER defense mechanism for KASLR incidentally impedes the attack, and the paper’s deployment conclusion is that KAISER must be deployed immediately.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: The abstract makes only a bounded claim about scope: "The attack works on different Intel microarchitectures since at least 2010 and potentially other processors are affected" — Intel microarchitectures are named, other vendors appear only as potentially affected, and this entry draws no conclusion beyond that. Success also depends on out-of-order execution itself, so it is not a software bug that can be patched away; the abstract puts the root cause in the hardware.
en.history: The arXiv record 1801.01207, "Meltdown", is authored by Moritz Lipp, Michael Schwarz, Daniel Gruss, Thomas Prescher, Werner Haas, Stefan Mangard, Paul Kocher, Daniel Genkin, Yuval Yarom and Mike Hamburg, submitted on Wednesday 3 January 2018 under cs.CR; the abstract itself is the primary record of this class of speculative-read attacks disclosed in early 2018.

zh: 乱序执行：为提升吞吐而打乱指令执行顺序的处理器特性。
副作用：推测路径上留下的微架构状态变化。
内核内存：操作系统保留的地址空间内容。
KAISER：摘要中被称为针对 KASLR 的防御机制。
KASLR：摘要中出现的内核地址随机化缩写。
权限无关读取：在不具备权限的情况下读出他方内存。
en: Out-of-order execution: reordering instruction execution to keep pipelines busy.
Side effect: microarchitectural state left by a speculated path.
Kernel memory: address space content reserved to the operating system.
KAISER: the defence mechanism the abstract describes as designed for KASLR.
KASLR: the kernel address randomisation named but not expanded in the abstract.
Unprivileged read: reading another party’s memory without permissions.
